s1.syndrome_frame: Sudden vision loss in one eye with optic disc swelling and retinal vascular occlusion
salient_findings: Sudden vision loss in the right eye
Right-sided relative afferent pupillary defect
Mild swelling of the optic disc
Peripapillary retinal hemorrhages
Occlusion of the superior branch artery
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 40s
Presented with blurred vision in the right eye
Undergoing treatment with systemic steroids, durvalumab, and bevacizumab
Developed sudden vision loss in the right eye 10 days after initial presentation
Visual acuity of 20/25 OU at initial examination
Right eye showed full visual field at initial examination
Right eye had marked swelling of the optic disc and peripapillary retinal hemorrhages at follow-up examination
Combined occlusion of the central retinal artery and vein
New collection of whitish material suspended anterior to the optic disc
Focal enhancement along enlarged right optic nerve on MRI
Diffuse enlargement of orbital portion of right optic nerve on MRI
Hyperintensity of right optic nerve on T2-weighted MRI
Lumbar puncture showed no abnormalities
Vitreous biopsy showed hypercellular sample with astrocytic neoplasm

shortlist.label: Optic Neuritis
shortlist.why_kept: Sudden vision loss and optic disc swelling

shortlist.label: Central Retinal Artery Occlusion
shortlist.why_kept: Combined occlusion of central retinal artery and vein

shortlist.label: Ischemic Optic Neuropathy
shortlist.why_kept: Sudden vision loss and optic disc swelling

shortlist.label: Giant Cell Arteritis
shortlist.why_kept: Optic disc swelling and retinal vascular occlusion

shortlist.label: Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Vitreous biopsy showed hypercellular sample with astrocytic neoplasm

raw.rationale: Vitreous biopsy showed hypercellular sample with astrocytic neoplasm, and immunohistochemistry results support a diagnosis of lymphoma, which explains the sudden vision loss and optic disc swelling

rejected.label: Optic Neuritis
rejected.why: Lack of typical symptoms such as pain on eye movement and absence of optic neuritis on MRI

rejected.label: Central Retinal Artery Occlusion
rejected.why: Presence of astrocytic neoplasm on vitreous biopsy and optic disc swelling suggest a more complex pathology

rejected.label: Ischemic Optic Neuropathy
rejected.why: Imaging and biopsy results indicate a neoplastic process rather than ischemia

rejected.label: Giant Cell Arteritis
rejected.why: Lack of typical symptoms such as headache, jaw claudication, and absence of giant cells on biopsy
